pr_body:
# Objective

- Fixes #13993

## Solution

- Add intermediate accesses to the running copy of `_access` in `AnyOf::update_component_access`

## Testing

- I've added a new test to make sure that `Query<AnyOf<(&mut A, &mut A)>>` correctly panics.

---

## Changelog

- Fixed `AnyOf` being able to cause undefined behaviour with conflicting accesses.

issue_context.title: `AnyOf` can violate single mutable alias rule

review_comments:
The comment should make it more explicit why this works. At first glance it might appear that this simply works because it's adding the access to the output `_access`, but actually `_access` will be replaced unconditionally at the end of the function by `_new_access`. The reason this works instead is because `_access` is cloned in the line 1871 (unfortunately I couldn't select it...), and by adding the access to it the later calls to `update_component_access` will see it and will be able to panic if they detect conflicting access. However this is not clear at all! Moreover the alternating use of `_new_access`, `_access` and `intermediate`, while necessary, is pretty difficult to reason with. IMO this really needs some better comments explaining how it all works and why it's ok.

Edit: at a second glance this also seems overconstraining, though I don't see a reasonable way to trigger the issue with the current `bevy_ecs`. If `With` and `Without` were usable in `QueryData`s you could write `AnyOf<((With<A>, &mut B), (Without<A>, &mut B))>` (well, in practice I don't think someone would want to do that, but never say never), which is fine but should result in conflicting access according to this fix.
I agree with the request for better comments. I also think this is overly constrained, but I'm very okay with restricting hypothetical uses for now to avoid UB.

I agree that in general access-related comments are sorely lacking. Every time I look at access-related code it takes me a super long time to understand why the code was written this way (generally subtle issues where we want to update the `read/write` access but not the `with/without` filters)

For example in this code, I don't get the purpose of the 
`_new_access.required = _access.required.clone();` line.
Is it because `required` shouldn't be updated at all, since none of the `AnyOf` components should be required? And we don't need it in the `_not_first` branch because  `append_or` and `extend_access` don't update `required`?

I think I found a way to make the change easier to understand: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/14013

@Gingeh let me know what you think
